title: Language-neutral detectors replace English built-ins
description:
As a policy author, I want rules written once with the language supplying its own words and units, so Spanish and Chinese packs are data and not branches in the engine.

Design: sections 2.2 and 2.3. Replaces the English-only built-ins (`passive_voice`, `overused_words`, `contrast_cap`, `list_shaped_prose`, length checks) with generic, parameterised detectors: `phrase` (word or substring matching by language), `regex` with a boundary token, `frame`, `density` against a per-language native baseline, `run`, `length`, `typography`. A rule the language cannot run is named in the coverage report, never skipped silently. If a language needs something the detectors cannot say, add a new generic detector, never a language branch.

Ryan 2026-11-13: a rule may drive rewrites (not only advise) once it is about 9 in 10 correct on held-out examples, measured per language, as a starting bar. A policy therefore carries its measured precision per language, and below the bar it only advises.

```gherkin
Feature: Rules are written once and take their words from the language
  Scenario: A density rule compares with what native writers do
    Given the Chinese language pack records how often native news uses the passive marker "被"
    And a policy that flags a paragraph using it far more often than that
    When Humanus checks a paragraph with five "被" in eighty characters
    Then the paragraph is reported with the measured rate and the native rate

  Scenario: A frame is found across a gap inside one sentence
    Given a policy for the frame "不是 … 而是"
    When Humanus checks "这不是一次简单的实验，而是一场深刻的变革。"
    Then the frame is reported once, from "不是" to "而是"

  Scenario: A rule the language cannot run is named, not skipped in silence
    Given a policy that needs word classes
    And a language pack without a tagger
    When Humanus checks a draft
    Then the coverage report names the policy as not run and says why

  Scenario: A rule drives rewrites only once it is right about nine times in ten
    Given a Chinese policy whose measured precision on held-out examples is 0.93
    And a Spanish policy whose measured precision on held-out examples is 0.78
    When Humanus offers fixes for a draft in each language
    Then the Chinese finding is marked as allowed to drive a rewrite
    And the Spanish finding is advice only
    And the precision is measured and stored per language, never shared between languages
```
